entry.title: Power of Habit

entry.content:
Every good thing should be a habit, and every bad thing turns out to be a habit as well.

Habit is such a great quirk. I lately realised that whatever productivity hunt or anti-procrastination drive we go on, habit is the only de-facto solution there.

How I noticed it#

I started realising this after reading the slides by yantar92 (Ihor Radchenko) for his EmacsConf 2026 talk, Personal task management under stress (with Org mode). He is the Org mode maintainer, and he does it in his spare time alongside a day job. I have been following him and attending the monthly Org meetup, and I am always astonished by how he even manages his life: so many emails on the Org mailing list that only he can take care of most of the time, work life, personal life, pending tasks and patches to review.

In the talk he outlines how tasks cannot be spread across different places like apps, the browser, email, your head, a notebook and maybe a phone call. They need one home. His first rule is simply "If you manage tasks in Org, do it in Org", and the second one is the one that stuck with me:

Task management won't work unless it becomes habit. Ever!

This is where Org mode and habit come into the picture.

The habit I already had#

I noticed that I often open reddit (r/emacs, r/OnePiece and so on), lobste.rs, mastodon and many more tabs to catch up every day and see what is happening. This has become so habituated that every day, without any effort, my hands naturally takes me there. It is a three times a day thing: morning, lunch and late night. That can be put down to media craving, but that is another topic.

The key thing to notice is that it has no obstacle. It is never missed, there is no holding back, and even at the busiest time there is at least a glance over it. That is my habit, and it connected all my GTD thoughts, productivity, self-help and everything else. From that moment I made sure, and even configured my system, to make it a thorough habit to capture notes, schedule tasks every day and just get on with them.

What a habit is made of#

Both popular books on this say roughly the same thing in simple words:

  • In The Power of Habit, Charles Duhigg describes a loop: a cue triggers a routine, and a reward tells the brain the loop is worth remembering. To change a habit, keep the cue and the reward and swap the routine.
  • In Tiny Habits, BJ Fogg says to make the new behaviour so small it needs no motivation, attach it to something you already do (an anchor: "After I …, I will …"), and celebrate it right away so it feels good.

Yantar's slides put the same idea in his own words: "Build new habits using existing habits". My tab ritual is a ready-made anchor. The cue (morning, lunch, night) and the reward (catching up) are already there, so the task habit only has to ride along with it.

Habits in Emacs and Org mode#

This is what that looks like in plain Org, nothing fancy. It is the same idea as my Art of Getting things Done post: start with defaults and let the system evolve.

Capture everything into one inbox#

The cheapest habit is capture. One key, one file, no thinking about where it goes. org-capture does this from anywhere in Emacs, and you sort it later. 

(setq org-capture-templates
      '(("i" "Inbox" entry (file "~/inbox.org")
         "* TODO %?\n%U")))
(keymap-global-set "C-c c" #'org-capture)
(keymap-global-set "M-k c" #'org-capture)
(keymap-global-set "s-k c" #'org-capture)
;; *-k since sounds like `K'apture

(keymap-global-set "M-j" #'org-agenda)
(keymap-global-set "s-j" #'org-agenda)
;; *-j since sounds like A`J'enda

The same inbox works on the phone with Emacs on Android or an Org app (bloom), and from the browser or elfeed or email notes.

Open the agenda before the tabs#

This is the anchor. Before reddit, open org-agenda (M-j). It takes a few seconds and it tells you what today actually needs. Yantar splits his day view into "Must do today", "May do today" and "Can do on a good day", which keeps a bad day from turning into a guilty one.

Open it anywhere, everywhere and anytime, make it a rhythm and make it a habit

Track the habit itself with org-habit#

Org has a built-in habit tracker. A habit is a TODO with a STYLE of habit and a repeater, and the agenda draws a small consistency graph next to it, so a broken streak is visible at a glance. 

(with-eval-after-load 'org
  (require 'org-habit))

* TODO Process inbox.org
  SCHEDULED: <2026-11-26 Thu .+1d>
  :PROPERTIES:
  :STYLE:    habit
  :END:
* TODO Catch up: r/emacs, lobste.rs
  SCHEDULED: <2026-11-26 Thu .+1d>
  :PROPERTIES:
  :STYLE:    habit
  :Effort:   0:20
  :END:

The second entry is my favourite idea from the talk: instead of fighting the distraction, give it its own habit with a time limit ("check social media (daily, once per day, 20 min max!)"). Clock in with C-c C-x C-i, and the Effort estimate tells you when to stop. A .+1d repeater means "one day after I last did it", and something like .+2d/4d allows a little slack for habits that are not strictly daily.

Review weekly, and plan to fall off#

Daily habits keep things moving, and a weekly review keeps the list honest. Group the someday tasks under projects or topics so the review stays short, and trim what no longer matters.

Habits also break: a trip, an illness, a busy month. Yantar's fourth rule covers exactly this: "First, go back to the habit of using your task management". Do not rebuild the system, just open the agenda again tomorrow.

Closing#

None of this needs a new app or a perfect setup. One plain text file (see Org mode is the best OBTF), one capture key, one agenda glance tied to a habit I already had. The tools only help once the habit is there.

Further reading#

  • Personal task management under stress (with Org mode) by Ihor Radchenko, EmacsConf 2026 (slides source, his Emacs config)
  • The Power of Habit by Charles Duhigg
  • Tiny Habits by BJ Fogg
  • Habit Stacking by James Clear
  • Tracking Habits with Org-mode on Worg
  • Org-mode and habits by Sacha Chua
  • Forming and maintaining habits using Orgmode by Charl P. Botha

entry.title: I've Consumed Enough
entry.summary:
I've had enough and Consumed enough these days.
From past days (…months actually) I've binged alot media and consumed so many free contents (just because they're free?). Movies, TV shows, Kdrama, Light Novels, Blog posts, Reviews (Movie/Books/Product), Comments on Reddit, Doom scrolling forum threads, Internet research and … I think I've just had enough. In the name of "Know it all person", I've just consumed and spent so much time on being Internet Nerd or Digital Consumer monster.
entry.content:
I've had enough and Consumed enough these days.

From past days (…months actually) I've binged alot media and consumed so many free contents (just because they're free?). Movies, TV shows, Kdrama, Light Novels, Blog posts, Reviews (Movie/Books/Product), Comments on Reddit, Doom scrolling forum threads, Internet research and … I think I've just had enough. In the name of "Know it all person", I've just consumed and spent so much time on being Internet Nerd or Digital Consumer monster.

Usually every time that we spend has some purpose, and yes I also had purpose to consume each bits. But at the end of the day, I finally want some answers, thoughts, moment of realization or insights that I'd carry.

Honest truth, Nothing really answered me, and only thing that kept back firing me was "Regret" on trying to do stuff by consuming them. I think I had well researched on things before, but still all I was procrastinate and go on consuming streak just so I don't miss on on-going things.

Eventually I realized that I only trying to kill time by pushing it ahead or trying to get motivated by external resources (again be it all media/content I mentioned). Sooner thankfully I finally realized that I only needed space and a moment to mindfully think whats actually needed and what I've been doing. You know, that moment or flow state of being self-conscious and understand whats surrounding you.

Majority of this related to me trying to perfect some PKM (Personal Knowledge Management) system and trying to write more blog posts. I tried Revamp the blogs so I'd be posting and writing more here.

Recently things have changed for good, thanks for me seeing the other side of ocean. Rather than looking at the book, I started looking at critics and review of things in negative side. Then it all clicked of whats wrong with current thoughts of people and media, golden tag I realized was that everyone is selling some or the other things. And people who buy well, proclaim it well, and only when you look at critic or product value we realize its not what it looks like.

One moment that clicked when I was reading on PKM was that not many successful people claim those fancy terms in practice, only people who are sold will advertise them. PKM or note taking has never been about a system, it was always about writing, thinking and processing, just that. They all just write than complicate or find a system. System comes when need exist, I don't think any practitioner has need for those fancy systems at all.

Another moment that clicked was when I stumbled across Lobste.rs Favorite Blogs discussion today. It showed how diverse poeple write posts and what they seek to communicate by them. Again realized here, most of them just write without boasting anything about organization or providing self-host to others. They'll just write to get it done, they don't validate with system to work for them. I Imagine they all achieve the Flow State while writing content and publishing, that is their formula for having it as favorite blogs. That flow state really dictates how quality they give out their posts.

Later this evening I stumbled on Abhinav tushar on mastodon and saw that he is part of Bangalore Indie web club. Did not know it existed at all, If not I'd have definitely made way to attend them as much as possible.

There is one things common from all people in that club, Weekly Posts, they all write weekly post on their own blog site. How the heck they write them all without missing or procrastinating? I thinking they all just start to write and get it done. Even as of writing this post I'm amazed at how everyone writes their every week. Even quality bloggers do only every month for one good post, and they all just write good enough.

I soon want to join their webring so it reminds me to write more so I get engaged in the club more. But I'll first try to attend in-person meetup and start getting disciplined myself to write more and then officially becomes the keeper.

Books are very verbose and beat around the bush (just because text is free). All books (from reviews) are better off an Article post, or One page or 21 lesson or 30 tips in summary. All books do is give out various examples to make readers self-validate the method and convey acceptance. Only when I look at critics part I realize the other way round. And Only thing book can give readers is to take a space/moment of time to reflect, think and process the information in concrete and pragmatic way. I believe One page a day only clicks for eliciting an idea or giving space for thoughts and processing.

Even I've not updated my blog site at all, stopped mid during adding media content in pages (Projects, Media and Wander My Small Web). I should start updating them since I read various gems from again recent consumption race.

  1. Brennan's take on PKM - Great site to read and writes alot
  2. BLR Indie Web Club - All posts + People blog page (so many writers)
  3. Dotat's two Decades of blogs - Good overview of how things changed and what remained constant trouble.
  4. …and there are more.

TLDR#

  • For anyone who couldn't grasp this post, What I wanted to say was that, I've wasted too much consuming media and resources all over Internet.
  • I've lately realized that I should start writing more or process information than being mindless consumer.
  • This time I'll finally put an end to mindless consumption and keep this post as reminder to do daily journal and write blog posts as much as possible.
  • I do not know who reads, so all I can do I hope to at-least do writing spree.

entry.title: Art of Getting things Done
entry.summary:
The tendency to organize things, and get the workflow in right track is a natural process, and we insist more on that in today's world. The mere idea of finding the "right way", "Best way possible" is a driving opinion for various Internet opinions. People do share what works for them, and they argue.
The ultimate deal I found is, a system does not have to help you, the natural process has to help you in getting things done.
entry.content:
GTD#

The tendency to organize things, and get the workflow in right track is a natural process, and we insist more on that in today's world. The mere idea of finding the "right way", "Best way possible" is a driving opinion for various Internet opinions. People do share what works for them, and they argue.

The ultimate deal I found is, a system does not have to help you, the natural process has to help you in getting things done.

Nowadays, the system has become a hindrance in workflow, like those popular apps trying to do that thing for you.

Usually to most of the person, GTD is not organized, it just goes hand in hand like a chain and workflow is mapped into our brain. Sure digital ecosystem has occupied and developed into a "Second brain" for us, but that should be too much work for first brain to train second brain to work perfectly for a system.

Just let go of the plans, just focus on what things to do for now. Slowly and gradually let your own system evolve that works perfectly for you, and there is no need to let the world know or judge about our system.

This snippet was addressed on the latest trends, and my long readings on articles and blogs over Zettelkasten, Getting Things Done, Personal Knowledge Management & Note-Taking.

This would be a never ending story, and ultimately I just sat with defaults without much over thinking the system or best practice. Just go with Org mode, plain text file with headings defined to make sense, add TODO for necessary tasks, and over a month, make changes if required to make it feasible and handy for next month. This worked great, I don't need complexity or automation for me to see at redundant information on my notes.
